# [Agentic Inference] Programmatic KV Cache for Agentic Workloads

# RFC: Programmatic KV Cache for Agentic Workloads

Authors: @ishandhanani, @hzh0425

## Introduction 

> [!NOTE]  
> Note: For this RFC, we will define “router” as an orchestrator on top of multiple engine units. 

Agent workloads make the value of a KV block predictable from above the engine, but that value is invisible to request-local LRU. We propose exposing a narrow, router-initiated hint surface so an external router can pass cache intent to SGLang without making invasive changes to the engine scheduler and cache manager. In this way, SGLang keeps ownership of scheduling and memory and is free to clip, defer, or reject any hint. 

Today the engine can identify cached content and local residency, but it does not know why a trajectory will reuse a prefix or how long an external tool/subagent gap will last. Session membership is useful metadata for lifecycle-scoped policies, but it is not the only way to address KV: request-scoped hints can name an exact token prefix after tokenization.

The session work in [](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27058) remains complementary. It lets the engine associate radix ownership with a session when the policy is genuinely session-scoped. The first L3 Pin POC described below is deliberately token-relative and does not require session identity.

With the work that is being done in PRs like 
1. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/20535 - allow for HiCache to become buffer mode and allow L3 cache to take more space on nodes. Buffer-mode isn't strictly required but the idea of giving L3 more memory is useful here
2. https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/2214 - allow for MC to start sending KV events which indexers can use

We can leverage L3 cache as the shared retention and movement substrate. The router expresses intent; SGLang resolves that intent against exact radix content and remains responsible for allocation, transfer completion, and visibility; the storage backend owns stored-object lifecycle.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    R["Router / orchestrator policy"] --> K["Provider-neutral KV hint"]
    K --> S["SGLang scheduler + HiCache"]
    S <--> G["L1: GPU KV"]
    S <--> H["L2: host KV"]
    S <--> M["L3: shared storage / Mooncake"]
    M -. retain now; share, prefetch, demote later .-> S
```

The hint surface is broader than any one backend operation. The concrete work so far validates one mapping—bounded Pin intent to a Mooncake L3 lease—without making that mechanism the whole RFC.

## High level roadmap (subject to change)

#### Phase 1 - session based kv cache
1. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29436 - enable a top level `session_id` so that we do not have to hijack `session_params.session_id` which is used for the `StreamingSession` cache
2. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27058 -  enable `session_id` to be tagged into kv blocks allowing us to refer to kv at the session level
3. TODO - enable `SessionRadixCache` to be implemented at the HiCache layer

#### Phase 2 - design router initiated hint API
1. POC implemented / PRs in progress - carry a provider-neutral `KvHintEnvelope` from an external orchestrator through request preprocessing and into the SGLang engine
2. POC implemented / PRs in progress - map bounded Pin intent onto exact committed HiCache page groups and a Mooncake L3 TTL lease
3. TODO - productionize admission, telemetry, expiry, namespace, and version-skew behavior for L3 Pin
4. TODO - measure request-time L3 restoration before adding proactive Prefetch or Demote execution APIs

## Problem Statement

The orchestrator knows the structure request-local policy cannot: which sessions are live, which token ranges are shared prefixes vs unique tails, which tool gap is 10ms vs 10min, when a subagent opened and closed. The engine sees a block hash and a refcount.

Current shape:

```text
request arrives
  -> router chooses target worker via KV overlap/load
  -> target worker checks local cache
       hit:  reuse
       miss: recompute or apply local offload policy
```

This is insufficient when: 
- another worker already holds the prefix; 
- the workload knows a request will resume soon; 
- a session has ended and its KV should be demoted/freed; 
- the orchestrator wants to protect high-value KV; 
- or local policy cannot tell a short tool gap from a long one.

The missing abstraction is a precise, observable surface where the orchestrator biases the cache manager without owning scheduler or memory internals. Letting an external system manipulate cache internals directly is the wrong design: it is brittle, it duplicates scheduler policy outside the engine, and it forces a refactor of the scheduler/cache-manager boundary. Hints keep ownership inside SGLang and let the orchestrator soft-influence behavior at request and lifecycle boundaries.

---

## Design Principles

1. **Orchestrator owns policy; engine executes.** The agent-graph / workflow intelligence lives outside. The engine understands priority, TTL, session membership, tier - nothing about why. Keeps things simple
2. **Zero overhead when unused.**  Un-hinted workloads behave exactly like today.
3. **Hints are soft, bounded, and safe to reject.** The engine may accept, clip, defer, or ignore. Every hint is observable. Nothing a client says can pin memory unboundedly or deadlock the scheduler.
4. **Router-initiated by default.** Workloads can still emit intent, but the router is where workload context merges with global KV placement, worker load, health, and admission. In production environments, the router has: a global KV index from events, built-in HA/fault-tolerance, existing overlap/load routing + admission control, and (with the harness<->orchestrator work) trajectory awareness, not just request awareness.

---

## Hint Taxonomy (conceptual)

### Share

Reuse a prefix that already lives on another worker or a shared tier: route a continuation to a less-loaded worker but pull the prefix from the old one; share a common prefix across sibling subagents; warm a scale-up worker. It is the existence proof for the whole model: the machinery to move KV natively between workers is what every other hint also needs. We can leverage L3 cache for this. 

### Prefetch

Move KV into a hotter tier *before* it is needed: warm GPU for a likely next-turn prefix; pull shared KV into a freshly selected worker; reload main-agent KV during a subagent's close. This is easily enabled after we get the APIs that the `Share` hint gives us.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant R as Router
    participant W as Worker
    participant L as Mooncake / L3
    participant H as HiCache host / L2
    participant G as GPU / L1
    R->>W: prefetch hint (exact prefix likely needed soon)
    W->>L: locate committed KV in shared L3
    L-->>H: stage KV into worker host cache
    H-->>G: promote only after transfer completion
    Note over W,G: SGLang owns allocation and radix visibility
    R->>W: continuation request arrives
    W->>G: cache hit, skip prefill
    W-->>R: tokens
```

### Demote 

Move KV to a colder tier instead of dropping it: long external tool call, paused trajectory, low-priority-but-reusable subagent state, memory pressure where recompute is expensive. Demote moves together with Prefetch/Onboard - the KV offloaded during a pause is the KV warmed back before the continuation resumes. This is easily enabled after we get the APIs that the `Share` hint gives us.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant R as Router
    participant W as Worker
    participant G as GPU / L1
    participant H as HiCache host / L2
    participant L as Mooncake / L3
    R->>W: demote hint (long tool gap, pause)
    W->>H: ensure the exact prefix is staged
    H->>L: ensure the prefix is published to shared L3
    Note over W,L: Publication and local reclamation are separate operations
    W->>G: allow local pages to become normally evictable
    R->>W: continuation resumes (paired prefetch)
    L-->>H: restore retained KV
    H-->>G: promote after completion
    W-->>R: tokens
```

### Pin

Keep a high-value prefix protected from ordinary eviction for a **bounded** TTL. Examples include expensive retrieved context, shared planner state, and tool/subagent gaps where recomputation dominates latency. A Pin hint should not imply permanent HBM residency: the engine may realize it at a colder tier while keeping L1/L2 normally evictable.

The first implementation POC realizes Pin at Mooncake L3:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client / agent harness
    participant R as Dynamo router
    participant S as SGLang + HiCache
    participant M as Mooncake L3
    C->>R: OpenAI prompt_cache_retention or Anthropic cache_control
    R->>S: Request + normalized prefix_tokens / ttl_seconds
    S->>S: Resolve exact committed, page-aligned prefix
    S->>M: Queue retain_groups(group_ids, ttl_ms)
    M->>M: Extend current members and future-member deadline
    Note over S,M: GPU and host copies remain normally evictable
    C->>R: Later continuation
    R->>S: Route normally
    S->>M: Existing request-time HiCache L3 lookup
    M-->>S: Retained KV pages
```

- [Mooncake](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/2835) adds TTL-bounded `retain_groups`, automatic expiry, future-member inheritance, and bounded group admission.
- Dynamo normalizes provider-native controls into a small `KvHintEnvelope`; SGLang resolves token offsets to exact HiCache page groups and queues the Mooncake metadata operation on its existing storage worker.
- A fresh MiniMax M2.7 H100 A/B evicted 24.18 GB / 95,232 keys under pressure. The unretained cold-worker probe recomputed 10,032 tokens; the one-hour retained probe restored 10,016 tokens from L3 and computed 16.
- This is "low hanging fruit" and can be used to implement Anthropic's `cache_control` API and OpenAI's `prompt_cache` APIs

The implementation uses “retention” because that is the provider API language. In this taxonomy it is a bounded L3 Pin. The Retain concept below remains priority-biased eviction rather than guaranteed lease protection.

### Retain

Bias eviction order rather than protect a prefix with a lease: some token ranges are worth more than others when eviction is unavoidable. The orchestrator attaches a relative priority (optionally with a duration) to a token range, and under memory pressure the engine evicts low-priority KV first. We have existing mechanisms to do this with the `priority` radix-cache strategy and can augment them with duration semantics similar to TensorRT-LLM's `TokenRetentionConfig`.

---

## Non-Goals

- Not a public user-facing cache API; the producer is the router/orchestrator.
- Not direct orchestrator manipulation of cache-manager internals; hints only bias.
- Not a replacement for local prefix matching or for sglang's LRU - it augments and reorders them.
- Not a guarantee the engine obeys any hint; accept/clip/defer/reject is always allowed.
- Not a commitment to freeze the current POC schema. `KvHintEnvelope { retention: [{prefix_tokens, ttl_seconds}] }` is the first exercised shape, not the final taxonomy.

---

## Relationship to existing SGLang work

This RFC is complementary to two in-flight SGLang efforts; it attacks the same agentic-KV problem from a different angle (a router above many engines) rather than from inside a single engine.

- **[](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/24656) - Agent-Aware KV Cache (Phase 1)** is the *in-engine, client-driven* angle: an optional `agent_hints` field on the OpenAI request flows into one engine, annotates radix nodes, and feeds an experimental `agent_aware` eviction policy. This RFC is the *router-initiated, multi-engine* angle on the same intent, and the two compose: #24656's `agent_hints` is the natural request-scoped envelope, and its `cache_ttl_ms` / `reuse_hint` are exactly our Pin / Retain hints. This RFC then adds the out-of-band control path and the cross-worker KV *movement* (Share / Prefetch / Demote) that #24656 explicitly defers (HiCache/storage metadata inheritance, cross-process coordination).
- **[](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/21846) - Distributed KVCache System for Agentic Workload** is the *mechanism / substrate*: HiCache tiering, PD incremental transfer, a storage prefetch interface, and hybrid-model support. This RFC is the *policy layer* that rides those rails - Share uses the worker-to-worker HiCache movement, Prefetch maps onto the roadmap's storage-prefetch interface, and Demote onto multi-tier offload. #21846 builds the plumbing; the router decides when to use it. Its own "Agent/Rollout KVCache Management" item already points back to #24656, so all three are one arc.

---

## References

<details>
<summary>External RFCs / APIs, research, and our prior work</summary>

External RFCs / APIs:
- vLLM #37003 - Context-Aware KV-Cache Retention API (Prioritized Evictions): (impl PR #38514)
- vLLM #37168 - Active Coordination and Two-Zone Scheduling for Long-Running Agents: (impl vllm-ascend)

- TensorRT-LLM `KvCacheRetentionConfig` / `TokenRangeRetentionConfig` (token_start/token_end/priority 0-100/duration_ms; default 35; decode_retention_priority; secondaryOffloadMinPriority)

Research:
- KVCache in the Wild (Alibaba traces): https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.02634

- KVFlow (workflow-aware prefix caching): https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.07400

Our prior work (sglang / Mooncake):
- #24656 (agent-aware KV phase 1 / API feedback), #21846 (distributed KV roadmap), #27058 (radix-native sessions), #27024 / #27025 (streaming-session deadlock + bound), #22273 / #21875 (streaming-session leak fixes), #18941 (TTL prefix pinning), #21045 (priority retention duration), [Mooncake](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/2214) (group semantics), [Mooncake](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/2835) (TTL-bounded group retention POC).

# [RFC] Agent-Aware KV Cache Phase 1 for Agentic Workloads

- Page: GitHub issue
- URL: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/24656
- State: open
- Author: stmatengss
- Created: 2026-05-08T03:40:31Z
- Updated: 2026-05-28T11:18:34Z
- Repository: sgl-project/sglang
- Number: #24656
- Comments: 10
- Assignees: huangtingwei9988

---

## Summary

This RFC proposes Phase 1 of agent-aware KV cache support in SGLang.

The goal of this phase is to add a minimal, backward-compatible metadata path for agentic workloads so workflow information can flow from the API layer into runtime requests and KV cache nodes, and optionally affect radix cache eviction.

This is intentionally a foundation/prototype phase, not a full workflow-aware cache system.

## Motivation

Current KV cache eviction policies such as LRU, LFU, and SLRU treat requests mostly independently. That works well for standard chat/completion workloads, but it misses reuse opportunities in agentic workflows, where requests often share:

- repeated prompt prefixes across planner/tool/worker steps
- parent/child step relationships
- short-term reuse after tool calls
- workflow-level TTL or reuse intent

Without workflow-aware signals, cache entries that are likely to be reused by upcoming steps may be evicted too early.

## Proposal

Phase 1 introduces:

- an optional `agent_hints` field in OpenAI-compatible requests
- propagation of `agent_hints` through the internal request pipeline
- lightweight workflow DAG tracking in the scheduler
- radix cache node annotation with workflow metadata
- a new optional radix eviction policy: `agent_aware`

Initial `agent_hints` fields include:

- `workflow_id`
- `agent_id`
- `step_id`
- `step_index`
- `total_steps`
- `parent_step_id`
- `children_step_ids`
- `tool_name`
- `expected_tool_duration_ms`
- `cache_ttl_ms`
- `shared_prefix_hash`
- `reuse_hint`

## Scope

Phase 1 is intended to cover:

- request schema support
- metadata plumbing
- scheduler-side workflow tracking
- cache node metadata annotation
- a prototype workflow-aware eviction strategy

Phase 1 does **not** attempt to fully solve:

- `shared_prefix_hash`-driven reuse
- HiCache / storage-layer metadata inheritance
- cross-process workflow coordination
- production-tuned scoring for all agent topologies

## Backward Compatibility

- `agent_hints` is optional
- existing clients do not need to change
- existing eviction policies continue to work unchanged
- the new behavior is opt-in

## Testing

Expected validation for Phase 1:

- schema tests for `agent_hints`
- propagation tests from API request to internal request objects
- workflow DAG tests for step registration and distance computation
- radix cache node annotation tests
- eviction ordering tests for `agent_aware`
- backward-compat tests when `agent_hints` is omitted

How to Run
Start SGLang with the new eviction policy:
```
curl http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "default",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hello"}],
    "agent_hints": {
      "workflow_id": "wf-1",
      "agent_id": "planner",
      "step_id": "step-1",
      "children_step_ids": ["step-2"],
      "cache_ttl_ms": 60000,
      "reuse_hint": "keep"
    }
  }'
```

Prototype validation already exists with dedicated unit tests for the metadata path.

## Open Questions

- Should `shared_prefix_hash` remain a hint, or become a stronger reuse primitive in a later phase?
- Should TTL be a hard protection or only a ranking signal?
- How should workflow-aware metadata eventually interact with HiCache and storage backends?
- What observability should be added next: workflow hit rate, protected eviction count, step-distance metrics?

## Requested Feedback

Feedback is especially useful on:

- the proposed `agent_hints` schema
- whether scheduler-local DAG tracking is the right Phase 1 boundary
- whether `agent_aware` should land as an experimental eviction policy first
- what should be included in Phase 2

# [RFC]: KV Cache Events for HiCache L3 Storage Backends - Page: GitHub issue - URL: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/29709 - State: open - Author: stmatengss - Created: 2026-06-30T03:52:14Z - Updated: 2026-07-02T02:49:29Z - Repository: sgl-project/sglang - Number: #29709 - Comments: 1 - Assignees: ishandhanani, huangtingwei9988 ## Labels - RFC --- | Field | Value | | --- | --- | | **Status** | Draft | | **Authors** | TBD | | **Created** | 2026-06-29 | | **RFC doc** | `docs/rfcs/kv-events-hicache-l3-storage-backend.md` (local draft) | | **Related** | [Mooncake RFC #1527](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/issues/1527), [Mooncake RFC #1403](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/issues/1403), [Dynamo #8912](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/8912), [Dynamo KV Events docs](https://docs.nvidia.com/dynamo/kv-managers/kv-events-for-custom-engines), [SGLang HiCache design](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/docs/advanced_features/hicache_design.md) | --- ## Motivation SGLang exposes **KV cache events** so cache-aware routers (e.g. `sgl-router` with the ZMQ cache-aware policy) can index which prefix blocks each worker holds and route requests accordingly. Today this pipeline covers: | Tier | SGLang medium | Event source | | --- | --- | --- | | L1 (GPU HBM) | `GPU` | Radix cache insert / load-back | | L2 (host pinned) | `CPU_PINNED` | HiCache write-through DMA ack | | L3 (distributed storage) | `EXTERNAL` | **Not emitted today** | When HiCache is configured with an L3 storage backend such as **Mooncake**, KV pages are written from host memory to the distributed pool after L2 backup completes. Routers and external indexers (Dynamo KV router, Mooncake standalone indexer) cannot see these blocks unless the engine or the storage backend publishes events for them. This gap breaks end-to-end cache-aware routing in deployments where: - Multiple workers share a Mooncake pool and any worker may prefetch from L3. - PD-disaggregation or decode-only nodes write decode output back to L3. - A cluster-level indexer needs a **multi-tier** view (`gpu` ≤ `cpu` ≤ `disk` / `external`) as described in [Dynamo #8912](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/8912) and [Mooncake RFC #1403](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/issues/1403). This RFC proposes how SGLang should close the L3 event gap, what metadata must flow through the HiCache storage interface, and how Mooncake (and other backends) participate. --- ## Background ### Current event flow (L1 / L2) SGLang records events in the radix cache via `KVCacheEventMixin` and publishes them from the scheduler: ```mermaid flowchart TD A["RadixCache._record_store_event(node, medium=...)"] --> B["tree_cache.kv_event_queue"] B --> C["SchedulerKvEventsPublisher.publish_kv_events()"] C --> D["ZmqEventPublisher (tcp://*:5557)"] D --> E["sgl-router / external indexer"] ``` L2 events are emitted when host backup completes: ```python # hiradix_cache.py — _finish_write_through_ack self._record_store_event(node, medium=StorageMedium.CPU) if self.enable_storage: self.write_backup_storage(lock_node, backup_len) ``` ### Current L3 write path (no events) L3 backup is asynchronous. On `ack_backup_queue` drain, SGLang only releases host protection and logs metrics — **no** `_record_store_event(..., medium=EXTERNAL)`: ```python # hiradix_cache.py — _drain_backup entry.release_host() # metrics only; no KV event ``` ### What storage backends receive today `HiCacheController.write_storage()` enqueues a `StorageOperation` with: - `hash_value`: page-level SHA256 hex strings (storage keys) - `token_ids`: full token sequence for the backed-up node - `prefix_keys`: optional ancestor keys (`hicache_storage_pass_prefix_keys`) The backup thread calls `storage_backend.batch_set_v1(keys, host_indices, extra_info)` where `extra_info` currently carries only `prefix_keys`. **Event semantics (parent hash, per-page tokens, depth, LoRA, medium) are not passed to the backend.** `StorageMedium.EXTERNAL` is already defined for Mooncake-class pools but unused in event emission: ```python class StorageMedium(str, enum.Enum): GPU = "GPU" CPU = "CPU_PINNED" DISK = "DISK" EXTERNAL = "EXTERNAL" # L4: shared / remote pool (e.g. Mooncake) ``` ### External standards [Mooncake RFC #1527](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/issues/1527) defines an engine-agnostic KV event wire format with envelope fields (`model_name`, `block_size`, `backend_id`, `medium`, `dp_rank`, …) and payload fields (`seq_hashes`, `parent_hash`, `token_ids`, `base_block_idx`). [Dynamo #8912](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/8912) adds multi-tier indexer support so lower-tier events (`cpu`, `disk`, `external`) are indexed rather than dropped. --- ## Proposal Adopt a **two-phase** approach: 1. **Phase 1 (engine-side events):** Emit `BlockStored` / `BlockRemoved` with `medium=EXTERNAL` from the radix cache when L3 backup completes (or when L3-backed pages are evicted). No Mooncake code changes required. 2. **Phase 2 (storage-side events + metadata plumbing):** Extend the HiCache storage interface so backends that own the L3 namespace (Mooncake master, standalone storage nodes) can publish conformant events. Pass per-page event metadata through `HiCacheStorageExtraInfo`. Both phases may coexist: the engine publishes events for blocks *this worker* wrote; Mooncake may additionally publish cluster-wide events for blocks written by any client. --- ## Architecture ### Tier event lifecycle (target state) ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph worker ["SGLang worker"] direction TB L1["L1 GPU"] E1["BlockStored(GPU)"] L2["L2 CPU"] E2["BlockStored(CPU_PINNED)"] L3["L3 EXTERNAL"] E3["BlockStored(EXTERNAL)"] MC["MooncakeStore.batch_set_v2(...)"] L1 -->|"insert / load_back"| E1 E1 --> L2 L2 -->|"write_through ack"| E2 E2 --> L3 L3 -->|"backup ack (Phase 1)"| E3 E3 --> MC end subgraph mooncake ["Mooncake"] POOL["Mooncake pool (DRAM / SSD)"] PUB["KvEventPublisher (Phase 2)"] POOL --> PUB end subgraph consumers ["Indexers"] ROUTER["Router / Dynamo indexer
(multi-tier: gpu, cpu, disk, external)"] end MC --> POOL E3 -.->|"engine ZMQ publisher"| ROUTER PUB --> ROUTER ``` ### Publishing responsibility matrix | Scenario | Recommended publisher | Rationale | | --- | --- | --- | | Worker writes prefix to Mooncake via HiCache backup | **Engine (Phase 1)** | Same pattern as L2; reuses existing ZMQ publisher and hash/token semantics | | Standalone Mooncake storage node receives PUT from any client | **Mooncake (Phase 2)** | Engine is not in the write path | | Mooncake evicts / TTL-deletes a page | **Mooncake (Phase 2)** | Engine may not observe the removal | | Worker prefetches from Mooncake (read-only) | **No store event** | Prefetch does not add new blocks to the worker's cache index | | Worker evicts host node whose data remains in Mooncake | **Engine remove(CPU)** only | L3 copy persists; optional `BlockRemoved(EXTERNAL)` only if L3 key is deleted | --- ## Interface changes ### Phase 1: Engine-side L3 events (minimal) **Emit on backup ack** in `HiRadixCache` / `UnifiedRadixCache`: ```python def _drain_backup(...): for operation in ack_backup_queue: entry = ongoing_backup.pop(operation.id, None) if entry is not None: node = entry # or (node, lock_params) in unified path if self.enable_kv_cache_events: self._record_store_event(node, medium=StorageMedium.EXTERNAL) entry.release_host() ``` **Emit on L3 key deletion** (if/when implemented): `BlockRemoved(medium=EXTERNAL)`. **Tests:** Extend `test_hiradix_cache_unit.py` / `test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py` L3 file-backend tests to assert `BlockStored` with `medium=EXTERNAL` after backup ack. No changes to `HiCacheStorage`, Mooncake, or event wire format. ### Phase 2: Metadata for storage-side publishing #### 2a. Extend `HiCacheStorageConfig` (init-time) Add fields passed when `StorageBackendFactory.create_backend()` constructs Mooncake: | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `page_size` | `int` | Tokens per block; maps to RFC `block_size` | | `backend_id` | `str` | Worker instance identity (hostname:port or pod UID) | | `dp_rank` | `int` | Attention DP rank for event attribution | | `tenant_id` | `Optional[str]` | Multi-tenant isolation (default `"default"`) | | `additional_salt` | `Optional[str]` | Opaque hash namespace salt ([RFC #1403](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/issues/1403)) | | `enable_storage_kv_events` | `bool` | Whether this backend should publish events | `model_name` is already present on `HiCacheStorageConfig`. #### 2b. Extend `HiCacheStorageExtraInfo` (per IO batch) ```python @dataclass(frozen=True) class KvEventPageMetadata: block_hash: int # hash_str_to_int64(hash_value[i]) parent_block_hash: Optional[int] # chain parent for this page token_ids: list[int] # tokens covered by this page base_block_idx: int # 0-based page depth in sequence lora_id: Optional[int] = None # from RadixKey.extra_key @dataclass class HiCacheStorageExtraInfo: prefix_keys: Optional[List[str]] = None extra_info: Optional[dict] = None kv_event_pages: Optional[List[KvEventPageMetadata]] = None medium: Optional[str] = None # "EXTERNAL" | "DISK" (SSD offload) ``` Built by `HiCacheController._page_backup()` from `StorageOperation.hash_value`, `StorageOperation.token_ids`, and `page_size`. #### 2c. Mooncake adapter changes In `MooncakeStore.batch_set_v1` / `batch_set_v2`: 1. On successful write, if `enable_storage_kv_events` and `extra_info.kv_event_pages` is set, call Mooncake's `KvEventPublisher` (new native API per [RFC #1527](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/issues/1527)). 2. Map Mooncake tiers: - Distributed DRAM segment → `medium="external"` (or `"cpu"` for Dynamo tiered indexer compatibility) - SSD offload (`enable_ssd_offload`) → `medium="disk"` 3. On backend-side eviction / TTL, emit `removed` events with `seq_hashes` + `base_block_idx`. #### 2d. Optional callback hook (backend-agnostic) For backends that cannot publish natively, add an optional callback on `HiCacheStorage`: ```python def on_kv_pages_stored( self, pages: list[KvEventPageMetadata], medium: str ) -> None: ... ``` The engine registers this to forward storage-side notifications into `kv_event_queue` when Phase 2 storage publishing is disabled but the backend wants to signal completion asynchronously. --- ## Hash and wire-format alignment SGLang events today use **SHA256 rolling page hashes** truncated to signed int64 (`hash_str_to_int64`). Mooncake RFC #1527 recommends **XXH3-64 (seed 1337)** rolling hashes. | Approach | Pros | Cons | | --- | --- | --- | | **A. Pass `token_ids`** in every event (current SGLang `BlockStored` already includes them) | Indexer can recompute with its preferred algorithm | Larger payloads | | **B. Align hash algorithms** across SGLang and Mooncake | Smaller events, direct hash matching | Breaking change for existing router index | | **C. `additional_salt` namespace** | Isolates tenants/models without hash migration | Does not unify algorithms | **Recommendation:** Keep SGLang's existing SHA256-based `block_hashes` for Phase 1 engine events. For Phase 2 cross-engine indexers, always include `token_ids` in storage metadata so Mooncake/Dynamo indexers can reconcile. Long-term hash unification is out of scope for this RFC and should be tracked separately against [RFC #1527](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/issues/1527). Existing SGLang ZMQ wire format (`BlockStored`, `BlockRemoved`, `AllBlocksCleared` via msgspec) remains unchanged in Phase 1. Phase 2 Mooncake-native publishing may use the JSON envelope from RFC #1527; a translation layer in the router is acceptable. --- ## Configuration ### Phase 1 No new flags. L3 events follow existing KV event config: ```bash --kv-events-config '{"publisher":"zmq","endpoint":"tcp://*:5557"}' --enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-storage-backend mooncake ``` ### Phase 2 (illustrative) ```bash --hicache-storage-backend-extra-config '{ "enable_storage_kv_events": true, "backend_id": "worker-0", "tenant_id": "default", "additional_salt": null, "kv_event_endpoint": "tcp://mooncake-master:6000" }' ``` Engine-side L3 events (Phase 1) remain controlled solely by `--kv-events-config`. --- ## Phasing | Phase | Scope | Deliverables | | --- | --- | --- | | **1** | Engine-side L3 events | `_record_store_event(medium=EXTERNAL)` on backup ack; unit tests; router can index L3 blocks written by this worker | | **2a** | Metadata plumbing | `KvEventPageMetadata`, extend `HiCacheStorageExtraInfo`, populate in `_page_backup` | | **2b** | Mooncake publisher | Mooncake native `KvEventPublisher`; adapter emits on set/remove; tier mapping (DRAM vs SSD) | | **2c** | Cross-project alignment | Map `EXTERNAL` to Dynamo indexer tier fields; document `additional_salt` / `cache_salt` forwarding | | **3** (optional) | Storage-side remove events | Mooncake TTL/eviction → `BlockRemoved(EXTERNAL)`; engine clears stale router entries | Phase 1 is independently shippable and unblocks cache-aware routing for HiCache + Mooncake without waiting for Mooncake RFC #1527 implementation. --- ## QA **Why not only emit events from Mooncake?** Engine-side emission (Phase 1) matches the existing L2 pattern, requires no Mooncake release, and attributes events to the correct worker/`dp_rank`. Storage-side emission is still needed for standalone storage nodes and cluster-wide eviction visibility. **Does prefetch from L3 emit a store event?** No. Prefetch loads data into L2 host memory; the router should already know the block exists at L3 from a prior store event. After prefetch, normal L2/L1 promotion events apply if the block is promoted to GPU. **How does this interact with MLA backup skip (tp_rank != 0)?** Only the rank that performs L3 backup should emit L3 store events, mirroring the existing MLA write-back skip. Other ranks must not duplicate events. **Will this duplicate events if both Phase 1 and Phase 2 are enabled?** Yes, unless coordinated. Default: Phase 1 on, Phase 2 off. When Mooncake publishing is enabled, disable engine-side L3 events via a flag (e.g. `engine_emit_l3_kv_events: false` in extra config). **Does this require hash algorithm changes in sgl-router?** No for Phase 1 — the router already consumes SGLang `BlockStored` with `medium`. Phase 2 Mooncake-native JSON events may require a new subscriber or adapter in the router. --- ## Open questions 1. Should `EXTERNAL` map to Dynamo's `disk` tier, a new `external` tier, or both (cumulative counts)? 2. Should engine-side L3 events be enabled by default when `--kv-events-config` is set, or require an explicit opt-in? 3. Who owns `event_id` monotonic sequencing when both engine and Mooncake publish for the same block? 4. Should `batch_set_v2` attach metadata on `PoolTransfer` instead of (or in addition to) `HiCacheStorageExtraInfo`? --- ## References - [SGLang HiCache design](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/docs/advanced_features/hicache_design.md) -
